rules.title: Explain arguments to another constructor
rules.before: The this() keyword can be parameterised or non - parameterised.
rules.after: Use this() to call another constructor without arguments, or this(value1, value2) to pass arguments. Java selects the matching constructor.
rules.reason: Distinguish a constructor call from the keyword and explain what the arguments do.

rules.title: Name the shared initialization constructor
rules.before: All other constructors can call that major constructor, passing default values or null references as arguments.
rules.after: Other constructors can call the constructor that performs shared initialization, supplying appropriate default values for arguments the caller did not provide.
rules.reason: Major constructor is not a Java term, and null is not an appropriate default for every field.

rules.title: Explain copying a reference
rules.before: We can copy that reference, as many times as we like, but there is still just one object that it might point / refer to.
rules.after: Copying a reference does not copy the object. Immediately after House second = first;, both variables refer to the same object.
rules.reason: Replace an uncertain relationship with a concrete assignment example.
